newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks swung back to gains Wednesday in brisk turnover which traders attributed to short-covering.

"The market digested options expirations and resumed its upward march after yesterday's drop, encouraged by lower U.S. long bond yields and by new strong industrial production data," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 2.0 percent to close at 817.02, erasing Tuesday's losses and setting a new five-year high.
"Even though the Dow fell today, U.S. treasuries are firm and yields may be heading for 6.5 percent, which should push the markets to new highs," Daneri said.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. bond eased to 6.69 percent from 6.72 percent at the opening.
Private consultants FIEL forecast industrial output growth of 5.2 percent in May against the same month of 1996, "which confirms the steady pace of recovery," Daneri said.
Floor volume rose to 39.4 million pesos in the session from 27.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover surged to 138.4 millon pesos from a puny 47.4 million Tuesday.
The broad market closed up 0.8 percent, with winners pounding losers 53 to 12 and 13 stocks closing flat.
The day's standout was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which shot up 10 percent on rumors the company will be either be sold or undergo drastic streamlining, dealers said.

Other top main-tier gainers were oil company Astra and steelmaker Acindar, which jumped 5.2 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively. The only MerVal losers were gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur and electricity generator Central Puerto, off 0.8 percent and 0.3 percent respectively.
